boards.school_name: The University of Texas at San Antonio
boards.title: Your First Weekend at The University of Texas at San Antonio, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A campus-first, under-21-safe sequence for learning UT San Antonio landmarks and traditions over a first weekend.

cards.title: Begin at John Peace Library
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Main Campus
cards.notes: Start at the Main Campus library, locate the front desk, and use the floor maps to pick a study spot or identify academic-support services for a later visit.
cards.short_summary: A practical first landmark with study space and campus services.
cards.evidence_claim: UTSA Libraries identifies the John Peace Library as located on the Main Campus and provides floor maps and building information.
cards.access_notes: Consult UTSA Libraries for current building access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Find the Sombrilla Fountain
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Sombrilla Plaza, Main Campus
cards.notes: Walk to the fountain outside the library and use the plaza as an orientation point. Take a photo from the walkway and leave the fountain structure undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: A central Main Campus landmark and documented Roadrunner tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio describes the Sombrilla Fountain as an iconic Main Campus landmark in Sombrilla Plaza near the John Peace Library.
cards.source_title: Being a Roadrunner | UT San Antonio Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; observe posted rules and do not enter or climb on the fountain.

cards.title: Meet Rowdy at the Roadrunner Statue
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Central Plaza, Main Campus
cards.notes: Continue to Central Plaza for a photo with the iron Rowdy sculpture. Try the documented Birds Up pose, but keep both feet on the ground and do not climb it.
cards.short_summary: A named mascot sculpture near the Sombrilla.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio identifies the Roadrunner Statue in Central Plaza near the Sombrilla and advises visitors not to climb on it.
cards.source_title: Photo Locations | UT San Antonio Commencement
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public artwork; photograph it without climbing or touching the sculpture.

cards.title: Use the Student Union as your reset point
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Main Campus
cards.notes: Stop at the information desk and look over current campus services, programs, and building wayfinding. It is a useful place to regroup before continuing your walk.
cards.short_summary: A Main Campus hub for student services and wayfinding.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio orientation materials identify the Student Union Information Desk as a helpful Main Campus location.
cards.source_title: UT San Antonio In-Person Orientation Experience
cards.access_notes: Services and building access may vary; check current Student Union information before arrival.

cards.title: Plan an active stop at the Rec Center
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Main Campus
cards.notes: Visit the Recreation Wellness Center to learn its layout and plan a future workout or recreation session. Bring required identification and verify entry eligibility first.
cards.short_summary: UTSA’s named Main Campus recreation facility.
cards.evidence_claim: UTSA Campus Recreation identifies the Recreation Wellness Center as a Main Campus facility and gives its campus-map location.
cards.source_title: Recreation Wellness Center | UTSA Campus Recreation
cards.access_notes: Check current facility hours, eligibility, and check-in requirements with Campus Recreation.

cards.title: Walk out to the UTSA Monuments
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · UTSA Oval, Main Campus
cards.notes: Use the Oval as a daylight walking destination and photograph the UTSA Monuments from the path. This is a clear checkpoint near the Main Campus entrance.
cards.short_summary: Named monument letters at the Main Campus Oval.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio identifies the UTSA Monuments as located at the UTSA Oval near the Main Campus entrance from Loop 1604.
cards.source_title: Photo Locations | UT San Antonio Commencement
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; use walkways and remain aware of campus traffic near the entrance.

cards.title: Cross the Bridge of Love
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · Arts and Flawn Sciences Buildings, Main Campus
cards.notes: Find the bridge connecting the Arts and Flawn Sciences Buildings, then take the documented campus-story walk across it with friends or a new roommate.
cards.short_summary: A named bridge tied to a documented UTSA campus legend.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio Student Affairs identifies the Bridge of Love as connecting the Arts and Flawn Sciences Buildings on the Main Campus.
cards.source_title: Being a Roadrunner | UT San Antonio Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Use the bridge normally and keep paths clear for people traveling between buildings.

cards.title: Learn the Birds Up hand sign
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · UT San Antonio tradition
cards.notes: Practice the official Roadrunner hand-sign instructions, then use it in a campus photo or when greeting fellow Roadrunners at an appropriate school event.
cards.short_summary: A documented UT San Antonio school-spirit gesture.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio documents the Roadrunner hand sign and explains how it is used to show school spirit.
cards.access_notes: Use the gesture respectfully; it does not require an event ticket or special equipment.

cards.title: Make a Downtown Campus stop at Bill Miller Plaza
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · Downtown Campus
cards.notes: If you are traveling to the Downtown Campus, make Bill Miller Plaza your meeting point and use it to orient yourself before exploring public campus pathways.
cards.short_summary: The central green-space landmark on UTSA’s Downtown Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio identifies Bill Miller Plaza as the green space at the center of the Downtown Campus where pathways intersect.
cards.source_title: Navigating UTSA: Your road map to get around campus | UT San Antonio Today
cards.access_notes: Plan transportation before leaving Main Campus and follow current Downtown Campus access guidance.

cards.title: Look for the Milagros hearts
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · Downtown Campus
cards.notes: While on the Downtown Campus, look closely at building facades for the bronze hearts in the Milagros art project. Observe the artwork without rubbing or altering it.
cards.short_summary: A documented campus art project of 31 bronze hearts.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio documents Milagros as 31 bronze hearts sculpted by alumna Diana Rodriguez Gil on Downtown Campus building facades.
cards.access_notes: View the exterior artwork from public areas and follow all posted campus access rules.
